title: THE GIANT · PRESS LADDER
vibe: GREEN · UPPER STRENGTH LADDER + BALLISTIC REDLINE — no treadmill, legs get a break from the pounding
why: You slept 7 hours, nothing is sore, and you want to bring it, so we bring it — just not into your legs or the treadmill. You have run a ~15:36 two-mile tempo in four of your last five sessions and yesterday you hammered your legs with heavy squats, a 40 lb chipper, and another 2-mile run. So today we finally break the running stack and give your legs, knees, and hips a real deload while your intensity goes UP top. The engine is a classic tactical press builder: 'The Giant' — single-arm clean and press climbed as a ladder — supersetted with heavy rows, so you push real strength on your shoulders and back (last real press day was 07-17, recovered now). Then a Tabata redline of snatches and swings for the glycolytic hit you're craving, all ballistic, almost no leg impact. It closes with get-ups — a pattern you have not trained since 07-11 — plus anti-rotation core. Mobility opens it, shoulders and spine today. Read as GREEN: climb the press ladders heavy, redline the Tabata. THERE IS NO RUN in this plan on purpose. If you truly cannot skip it, make it a genuine easy 1-mile shakeout at 6.0 mph — NOT a fifth tempo. That is the whole point of today.

blocks.title: MOBILITY WARM-UP
blocks.meta: ~10 min · standing rule · shoulders + spine biased (press day)
blocks.text: Pulse first: easy jog OR jumping jacks / arm swings 3 min to warm up. Original Strength resets: diaphragmatic breathing x5 · head nods + rotations 5 each · quadruped rock-backs x10 · cross-crawls 10/side. Then open the shoulders and spine for pressing (Moves Method Day A): shoulder dislocates / band or towel pass-throughs x10 · thoracic rotations (quadruped or open-book) 6/side · scapular CARs 5/side · wall slides x10 · thread-the-needle 5/side · pec-opener doorway stretch 30s · wrist rocks 10. Finish with 2 rounds of 5 strict presses with the 16 kg per arm to groove the overhead lockout. Shoulders do the work today — get the overhead position fully open and the T-spine moving before you load the ladder.

blocks.title: THE GIANT · CLEAN + PRESS LADDER
blocks.meta: ~18 min · 40 lb single + 50 lb DB · push the load, grind the reps
blocks.format: ASCENDING LADDER 1-2-3-4-5 · superset with a heavy pull · RPE 8
blocks.workRest: Climb one full ladder per arm, then a set of rows. Repeat for as many full ladders as you can in ~18 min (target 2-3). Rest as needed to keep the presses clean.

items.name: A1 · 1-Arm Clean & Press (ladder)
items.detail: 40 lb · climb 1→2→3→4→5 reps, LEFT arm, then the same 1→2→3→4→5 RIGHT arm = one full ladder. Re-clean every rep. Strict overhead lockout, no leg drive.

items.name: A2 · Bent-Over Row
items.detail: 50 lb DB · 8-10 per side after each full press ladder · flat back, drive the elbow past the ribs, own the squeeze

blocks.text: 'The Giant' is the tactical/military press builder — high-quality overhead volume climbed as a ladder so you accumulate real pressing strength without one crushing set. Clean the bell fresh for every rep. Use the zip-up brace on every press: grip the floor with your toes, flex the quads, squeeze the glutes, brace the abs like you're about to take a punch, tighten the lat to lock the armpit — then press strict, no bend or dip in the legs. That full-body tension is what makes a heavy press feel light. The rows between ladders balance all that pressing with heavy pulling so your shoulders stay healthy. This is where today's strength intensity lives — climb it heavy, and if 5 reps at the 40 gets grindy, that's the point; just keep the lockout honest. If your left is weaker, climb to whatever top rung it owns cleanly and match the right to it.

blocks.title: TABATA REDLINE
blocks.format: TWO TABATAS · ballistic · almost zero leg impact
blocks.workRest: Tabata = 8 rounds of 20s all-out / 10s rest = 4 min each. Rest 2 min between the two. Count total reps if you want a score to beat next time.

items.name: TABATA 1 · Snatch
items.detail: 16 kg · 8 × (20s on / 10s off) · switch arms each round (or at the halfway rep). Punch the bell overhead, snappy, all hips.

items.name: TABATA 2 · Two-Hand Swing
items.detail: 16 kg · 8 × (20s on / 10s off) · float to chest height, hard hip snap, crisp lockout at the top

blocks.text: This is your redline — the hard glycolytic hit you wanted, delivered ballistically so your legs and knees stay out of the pounding. Snatches drive the shoulders and posterior chain and spike the heart rate fast; the swing Tabata keeps the engine pinned while sparing your already-fried pressing muscles. Go all-out in the 20s windows — that's where the fat-loss stimulus lives — and use the 10s to reset your grip and breath, not to quit. If your grip is the limiter on the snatch (likely after the ladder and rows), park the bell for a second rather than losing the overhead lockout. Two Tabatas, eight minutes of work, and you'll be smoked without a single running step.

blocks.title: GET-UP + CORE FINISHER
blocks.meta: ~10 min · get-up (neglected pattern) + anti-rotation · standing rule

items.name: Turkish Get-Up
items.detail: 16 kg · 1-2 per side · move slow, pause at each position, eyes on the bell — full-body midline under load

items.name: Side Plank
items.detail: 30s per side · stack the hips, reach the top arm tall, no sag — anti-rotation

items.name: Hollow Hold
items.detail: 30s · ribs down, low back pressed flat to the floor — anti-extension

blocks.text: Your end-of-session midline block, built around the get-up — a pattern you have not trained since 07-11, so it was overdue. The get-up is a full-body, shoulder-stabilizing grind that ties the whole session together and keeps your overhead pressing durable; go slow and own every transition. Side plank and hollow cover anti-rotation and anti-extension — the core work that keeps your back happy under all that overhead load. Three clean, deliberate rounds. If the 16 kg get-up feels easy, load it to the 40.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN
blocks.text: Walk 2 min to bring the heart rate down. Then decompress everything you pressed: overhead lat stretch (hang on a doorframe or reach-and-side-bend) 30s/side · cross-body shoulder stretch 30s/side · doorway pec stretch 30s/side · thread-the-needle 30s/side · child's pose with a side-reach 45s · 5 slow breaths. Reminder: today is a deliberate NO-RUN day to deload your legs — if you absolutely have to run, keep it an easy 1-mile shakeout at 6.0 mph, not a tempo.
